required_fixes.issue: The course outcome transforms explicitly includes the z-transform and pole-zero geometry, but the only module claiming that outcome is Fourier Representation and Computation. The lessons that introduce z-transform and pole-zero-model are in Filter Design and Implementation, whose outcomes list omits transforms.
required_fixes.required_change: Either add transforms to Filter Design and Implementation, move the z-transform result into a module that claims it, or narrow the outcome text so every claimed part is delivered by a claiming module. Preserve the current lesson prerequisite order.

required_fixes.issue: Fifteen concepts introduced by non-extra lessons have fewer than three declared encounters across concepts.introduces and concepts.reinforces. Their use may be implicit in goals or key ideas, but C5 requires the revisits to be visible in course.yaml.
required_fixes.required_change: Declare substantive revisits in existing later lessons and applications, or consolidate a concept that is not meant to be independently retrieved. Do not add padding lessons solely to increase counts; each added reinforcement must appear in the lesson goal, key ideas, application, or planned mixed exercise.

required_fixes.issue: The approved coverage proposal classifies perfect-reconstruction and wavelet/filter-bank matrix theory as an advanced off-path branch. The final structure makes Perfect-Reconstruction Filter Banks core, elevates it to a headline key result, and makes two later core lessons depend on it. This turns specialist Vaidyanathan/JOS/MIT 6.341 material into a gate for communications and quantization.
required_fixes.required_change: Restore the proposal boundary: make the rigorous PR-bank branch extra and remove it from every core prerequisite chain. Teach only the minimal non-gating subband model needed by the core communication application, or move subband allocation with the filter-bank branch into an extra. Remove or replace the PR headline key result if it is no longer core.

required_fixes.issue: The research proposal contains a notation ledger, but its first_lesson references use proposal IDs such as l01-discrete-signals and l21-stft rather than the final course slugs. The final planning files therefore do not provide an actionable per-lesson ledger for symbols, spoken forms, domains, examples, and common confusions.
required_fixes.required_change: Re-key the companion notation ledger to the final lesson slugs and add one concrete example per family before lesson drafting. Surface each family at the lesson where it first lands, and carry explicit translations for source normalization, sign, centering, and PSD conventions.

warnings.message: The first lesson is the unique 32-minute minimum and is clearly gentle. The second lesson is explicitly polished and has a concrete three-tap win, but it introduces LTI system, impulse response, and convolution plus an identification demo in 36 minutes. Pilot it as an opener and keep the demo scaffolded; the design proposal's even gentler sampled-sinusoid opener was not used.

Quantization, Dither, and Subband Allocation remains one coherent rate-distortion evaluation, but it introduces two concepts and reinforces four while combining overload, statistical error, dither, and band allocation. Preserve one decision throughline and move optional derivations to starred sections rather than splitting into micro-lessons.

All 15 demo specs pass D1 on paper: each has a manipulation, target or threshold, and a claim to falsify. Responsiveness, accessibility, initial presets, and the approximately 200-line implementation budget cannot be verified until components exist.

All five modules end in real applications that name results and idealization gaps. The recorded-audio and final-link applications still condition their artifacts on rights-cleared recordings, so asset provenance must be resolved before drafting figures or distributing audio.
